characters: Iddi: a boy of six with big eyes, a yellow T-shirt and a gap in his front teeth.
Nurse Manu: the school nurse, in a white coat, holding a big toothbrush and a model of a mouth.
The sugar bugs: tiny cartoon germs with silly faces, drawn as friendly and not scary, wearing little party hats.

narrationPlan.voice: A cheeky boy’s voice for Iddi; a warm, no-nonsense school nurse’s voice
narrationPlan.pace: Playful, with a wince at the toothache and a cheer at the end (about 90 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: A bouncy, comic tune with a drum roll at the toothache (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Iddi, Nurse Manu and the family are invented. The story teaches the habits of brushing in the morning and at night, using a little toothpaste, eating fewer sweets and visiting a dentist.

“Sugar bugs” is a simple picture for the germs in the mouth that feed on sugar and make acid that damages teeth; the story says “tiny germs”. It does not suggest that sweets are bad in small amounts or that families who cannot afford a dentist are at fault; teachers should be sensitive to this.
Some families clean teeth in other ways; teachers should ask local health workers for advice and not criticise a family’s practices.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Have a dentist or a school health nurse check the explanation of germs and sugar, the brushing advice (morning and night, a little toothpaste, about two minutes) and the sentence about fewer sweets.
Check that the story is sensitive to children who do not have easy access to a dentist or toothpaste.

teacherGuide.overview: A funny story that teaches simple tooth care. It uses cartoon “sugar bugs” to explain why sugar and brushing matter.
learningGoals: Say two things that help keep teeth healthy.
Say why too many sweets can hurt teeth.
beforeReading: Ask: what do you do to keep your teeth clean?
whileReading: Wince on page 3 and cheer on page 8.
afterReading: Practise brushing on a model mouth with a big toothbrush.
Make a chart of “fruit and water” snacks.
discussion: Why did the nurse draw sugar bugs with party hats?
What can Iddi eat instead of sweets?
reflection: What is one habit you want to keep every day?

support: Use picture cards for brush, toothpaste, fruit and dentist.
stretch: Draw a tooth-care poster for the classroom door.

Some families clean teeth in other ways; teachers should ask local health workers for advice and not criticise a family’s practices.
localiseThis: Ask a local health worker how families in your area look after their teeth and what a visit to the dentist costs. Do not shame any child for the state of their teeth.

factCheck.claim: Germs in the mouth feed on sugar and make acid that damages teeth; brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, eating less sugar and visiting a dentist help to protect teeth.
factCheck.reference: World Health Organization or Ghana Health Service oral health guidance (to verify).
